title: Concerning the Fourteen Vehicles that Jesus has boarded.
text:
⟨p.36⟩
VIII
— Concerning the Four Mounts —
VIII which Jesus mounted upon VIII
Again the Man of Light speaks to the {6} sits before
him, saying: When Jesus the Son of the Greatness {7} to the world{8},
at the time when he was disclosed of the Greatness, {9}
mounts. He walked in the world {10}.
The first mount is the vessel of light, {11}
he received commandments from the Ambassador {12}.
⟨p.37⟩
The second chariot is the abode of the First Man, since
the tabernacle is established in him.
The third is the Pillar of Glory, the Man who is perfect, since
he shone forth in him, came down, was made manifest in the
world. The fourth is the Call that he wore
upon his body. The fifth is the Answer that he donned
upon the Call. The sixth is the living Air; since
he himself also wore him, he received anointing in him.
The seventh is the living Wind that breathes. The eighth
is the Light that radiates light. The ninth is the Water that
lives. The tenth is the Fire that lives, that is mingled in them all.
His walking is in this ten of chariots, in all the forms and in the
{0}, all those of above and those of below.
After he wore this ten, he came, he was unveiled in the
flesh; he chose the holy Church in four mounting-
places. The first is all the holy brothers; the second is the
pure sisters; the third is the catechumens
all, the sons of faith; the fourth is the catechumen-
ae, the daughters of the Light and of the Truth. This ten of char-
iots upon which he mounted in the Girdle, with the other four that are in the flesh,
they are completed and become twelve chariots — those that he wrought in them —
the intent of his Father. He raised to life, he ransomed, he gave the victory to
{1}those who are his own; he himself killed, bound, destroyed
those who were strangers to him. He gave them to the Father who sent him,
with the whole kingdom of life forever, to him who shall
know the mysteries; that he be reckoned to the honor of Jesus,
the Son of the Greatness.
